text.insert: The persisted jobs table records executable requests so consumers can claim work, retry failures, and recover after a restart. Job status describes execution; the result reference points to the domain record that explains what was produced.

rows: Identify the executable request and its game or run. The kind and dedupe key pair is unique.
Status is queued, claimed, running, waiting, succeeded, failed, or cancelled. Revision guards concurrent updates.
Execution class is local or sandbox. A fenced job claim and expiration govern one consumer's work.
Persist attempt count, retry eligibility, small input parameters, and references to results or failure details.
Connect accepted job changes to trace evidence and timestamps.

text.insert: Retry limits and backoff are consumer policy; they are not max_attempts or backoff columns in this table. Job leases are distinct from the game's Dispatch State lease. A claimed background job does not independently authorize protected checkout mutation.

Run records own claims, workers, epochs, and integration outcomes. Knowledge records own source material, attempts, facts, and evidence. Jobs retain the request and execution result reference without absorbing those domain records.

One consumer serializes claim ticks while allowing jobs to execute up to the descriptor's concurrency limit. The default tick interval is one second. A claim predicate can suspend new work without rewriting queued jobs.

text.insert: Execution and settlement hooks are tracked separately. The default settlement warning starts after 60 seconds, and shutdown waits up to 120 seconds for pending settlement hooks.
